tagline: The most charming village on the Asian shore — wooden Ottoman houses, a synagogue, church, and mosque on the same street, and the best Sunday morning walk in Istanbul.

items.name: İçerenköy Kahvaltı / Kuzguncuk Cafés
items.description: The main street (İcadiye Caddesi) has excellent independent cafés serving Turkish breakfast. On Sunday mornings this is one of Istanbul's loveliest scenes.
items.tip: Sunday morning breakfast here, then a walk along the waterfront to Üsküdar — this is an ideal half-day on the Asian side.

items.name: Kuzguncuk Bostanı
items.description: A community garden with a small café operating in the warmer months. Beautifully local and completely off the tourist trail.

items.name: Meyhane Kuzguncuk
items.description: Several excellent meyhane (traditional tavern-restaurants) on and around İcadiye Caddesi. Mezes, fish, and raki in garden settings.
items.tip: Go for a long lunch rather than dinner — the garden settings are better in daylight.

items.name: İcadiye Caddesi Walk
items.description: A stroll down the main street past wooden mansions, the historic synagogue, the Greek church, and the mosque — all peacefully coexisting on the same road.

items.name: Kuzguncuk to Üsküdar Waterfront
items.description: A beautiful 20-minute walk south along the Bosphorus from Kuzguncuk to the Üsküdar ferry landing. One of Istanbul's finest waterfront walks.

tips: Kuzguncuk is a 20-minute walk north from Üsküdar ferry landing, or take a dolmuş from Üsküdar.
Sunday morning is the best time — the village is calm, cafés are full, and the atmosphere is magical.
Almost no tourists visit. This is one of the most authentic neighbourhood experiences left in Istanbul.
Combine with Üsküdar for a full Asian side day — walk the waterfront between the two.
